hint.label: Activist
hint.text: An activist is someone who wants to make a change in society.

atoms.text: This is Millicent Fawcett, a famous activist, who tried to help women win the right to vote.

instruction.text: You’re talking with Millicent. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: How did you help ((men ++women)) get the right to vote?
I created a group for upper class women called the National Union for Women’s Suffrage Societies in ((2016 ++1897)).
We held protests, but made sure they were peaceful so that the government would ((hate ++respect)) us and give us the right to vote.

instruction.text: Build the portrait of this famous suffragette.

feedback.end: Emmeline Pankhurst was also a member of the National Union, but she started to get annoyed with their lack of progress. She didn’t believe that peaceful protests were going to help them win the vote.

atoms.a: In 1903, Emmeline decided to begin her own movement that ...
atoms.sound: In 1903, Emmeline decided to begin her own movement that welcomed all women.

atoms.a: She used the motto “deeds not words” because they used ...
atoms.b: actions instead of peaceful protests to try to win the vote.
atoms.sound: She used the motto “deeds not words” because they used actions instead of peaceful protests to try to win the vote.

atoms.a: Her movement was called the Women’s Social and Political Union, but...
atoms.b: they were better known as the suffragettes.
atoms.sound: Her movement was called the Women’s Social and Political Union, but they were better known as the suffragettes.
